source: direct adjudication of residue_batches/batch_006.json (the batch_026 dispatch hole: built, never dispatched, so the two twin_shaped cases came back unruled from pass 3)
evidence: the two packets in residue_batches/batch_006.json, with every count, month label, footprint and identity field re-verified against state/observations/agency_year_observations.parquet and state/reference/agency_to_jurisdiction_crosswalk.parquet before ruling

rulings.detail: same_agency_merge. Canonical ORI9 = CO0340500; CO034019E collapses into it. One agency -- Fort Lewis College Police Department -- surfacing under two ORI9 keys in DIFFERENT ORI7 blocks (CO03401 vs CO03405), which is exactly why the deterministic stem rule cannot reach it: build_cross_lane_twin_ledger pairs on ori7_stem. 2024 mass is 29, once, on 08:statewide_overlap_layer; the panel currently carries 29 twice (CO034019E NIBRS 12mo, CO0340500 CIUS 12mo and SRS 11mo). The merge is retrospective across 2018-2024, not 2024-only. REVERSES the canonical named by the pass-1 registry row (CO034019E): direction is variant(NIBRS, non-...00) -> canonical(...00), the same direction the twin rule uses and for the reason the rule states -- CO0340500 is the key whose identity is already resolved (agency_name_std FORT LEWIS COLLEGE, agency_name_raw 'fort lewis college', crosswalk_agency_name 'fort lewis college police department', place_fips 22035 = Durango city, ori7 CO03405), while CO034019E carries agency_name_std DURANGO from the NIBRS batch header's city_name with agency_name_raw, crosswalk_agency_name, place_fips and ori7 all null. Merging the other way publishes a campus agency as DURANGO -- the Rancho-Cordova-named-SACRAMENTO pathology the identity module exists to remove. Mass is unaffected by the reversal: both members are crosswalked w=1 to the same footprint, so 29 lands once either way, and the surviving lane selection is unchanged. Verdict token also corrected from superseded_ori: CO0340500 is not dead -- it carries a 2024 SRS row at 11 months and a 2024 CIUS row -- and its footprint is the statewide overlap layer, not exclusive municipal ground, so neither leg of the succession rule (stale-by-recency, municipal weight-1.0 coverage) reaches it. The repair is a dedupe, not a fill suppression.
rulings.rationale: Deciding fact, verified against the panel and not taken from the packet text: the two ORIs' seven-offense vectors are identical in all seven years 2018-2024 (totals 25/32/12/18/23/24/29; per-offense byte-identical, the single exception being 2018 aggravated assault 2 in CIUS against 0 in SRS and NIBRS, a publication-vintage difference inside one submission), while CO034019E's NIBRS months are 12 throughout and CO0340500's Return-A months are 10/11/10/10/11/12/11 -- one NIBRS submission back-converted into Return-A under a second ORI key, with month labels derived from which months carried incidents. Seven consecutive years of unit-exact agreement across seven offense streams is not reachable by coincidence. Corroboration: same state and county (08/067), same footprint, CO0340500's own crosswalk name is 'fort lewis college police department', and the 2024 roster names CO034019E 'Fort Lewis College' (University or College, La Plata, NIBRS start 2004-07-01) while CO0340500 is absent from it. Absolute plausibility rules out the surface reading of the names: Durango PD serves about 19,000 residents and would report hundreds of Part-I offenses a year; 12-32 a year on a rape-and-larceny mix with FBIpop 0 is the college. REPORTED, NOT DECIDED HERE: the surviving footprint is wrong under any policy -- both keys sit w=1 on the Colorado statewide overlap layer because CO0340500's census_name joined to 'state of colorado', so one college campus is smeared across Colorado; that is a Stage-2 crosswalk-policy item and this ruling leaves it untouched. Also noted: CO0340500 is off the 2024 roster, which is what benchmark_imputation reads for its defunct-vs-non-reporting split -- harmless in 2024 because the merged agency has an observed value, but the merged identity is an off-roster key.

rulings.detail: distinct_agencies. Keep all three ORI9s -- CA0409940, CA0409945, CA0409901. No member collapses; the group's 34 counts for 2024 are correct as reported and there is no double count to remove. All three stay w=1 on 06:statewide_overlap_layer, unchanged. Consequence recorded for the queue: because the CA04099 area offices are separate agencies, the unit of a zero/token disposition is the individual ORI, so the pilot-era three-ORI bundle c-CA0409945-chp-san-luis-obispo (CA0169940;CA0409945;CA0479945 -- three offices in three different ORI7 blocks, grouped by that reviewer as a shared-submitter family and not as an identity claim) is authoritative only for the ORI that has no per-ORI ruling of its own, CA0409945. CA0409945's 2024 level question (101 -> 8) is a token-reporting question, already answered token_reporting_flag by that row, and is not evidence for a merge.
rulings.rationale: Deciding fact: the FBI 2024 roster lists all three ORI9s as separately named CHP commands with their own mandates -- CA0409940 'Highway Patrol: Templeton Area Office', CA0409945 'Highway Patrol: San Luis Obispo Area Office', CA0409901 'Highway Patrol: Coastal Division' -- all State Police, San Luis Obispo county, all NIBRS-active from 2021-11-01, so the shared ORI7 block is CHP's internal numbering of one division's offices rather than one agency filing three ways. Verified against the panel: the members' totals diverge year on year (2021 partial 6/18/0, 2022 42/102/2, 2023 14/101/0, 2024 25/8/1) and no member equals or contains the group sum in any year, so CA0409901 is not a rollup parent and no member is a partial rendering of another -- the identical-vector merge rule correctly did not fire, and there is no cross-lane split here at all (every member reports through NIBRS only). Consistent with the two CHP block cases already adjudicated on the same evidence shape: a2-CA01999 (14 members) distinct_agencies and a2-CA04799 distinct_agencies. REPORTED, NOT DECIDED HERE: all three sit w=1 on the California statewide overlap layer, so 34 counts are smeared statewide instead of landing on San Luis Obispo County highway ground -- the same state-police footprint question Stage 2 settled for KY/WV/VT/RI and left open for CA; CA0409901's crosswalk row already carries review status flagged_auto.
